subject: diplomatic-appointments-lqa
note: 2A, 2026-10-02, for confirmation at 3H. Every express cross-reference in the Bill, and the unwritten reliance on the Acts Interpretation Act, the Legislation Act and the Constitution (0H items, named by id in 'to'). Modules named for 'encoded' entries are planned paths, written at 4A; none exists yet. All entries are at depth 1: no finding exists yet that would justify going deeper.

entries.from: s 2(1), table item 1 ('The day after this Act receives the Royal Assent')
entries.to: Acts Interpretation Act 1901 s 3A (commencement at the start of the day) and s 36 (calculating time) [0H: cth-acts-interpretation-act-1901]

entries.from: s 4 ('applies both within and outside Australia and extends to every external Territory')
entries.to: Acts Interpretation Act 1901 s 2B ('Australia', 'external Territory') [0H: cth-acts-interpretation-act-1901]
entries.reason: extraterritorial application does not change whether an appointment complies; the offices in s 7 are outside Australia by nature, so the encoding assumes the Act reaches them

entries.from: s 5 (Crown to be bound)
entries.to: Acts Interpretation Act 1901 s 2A (binding the Crown) [0H: cth-acts-interpretation-act-1901]
entries.reason: s 5 states expressly what s 2A would otherwise supply; read at 9A if a finding turns on whether the Bill binds the Governor-General or the prerogative (see REF-18)

entries.from: s 6 ('Minister means the Minister administering the Diplomatic and Consular Missions Act 1978'), and every use of 'the Minister' in ss 9-14
entries.to: Diplomatic and Consular Missions Act 1978 (whole Act, as the identifier of the Minister) [cth-dcma-1978]; Administrative Arrangements Order of 13 May 2025, Part 8 (DFAT) [cth-aao-2025]; Acts Interpretation Act 1901 s 19, table item 2 ('the Minister, or any of the Ministers, administering that law') [0H: cth-acts-interpretation-act-1901]
entries.reason: who the Minister is on a given day is set by the Administrative Arrangements Order and by which Ministers are sworn to administer DFAT, not by the Bill; the encoding takes the Minister's identity as an input. The DCMA itself confers no power the Bill relies on (it concerns false claims of diplomatic status in Australia)

entries.from: s 6 ('Secretary means the Secretary of the Department administered by the Minister')
entries.to: Acts Interpretation Act 1901 s 19A (references to Departments) [0H: cth-acts-interpretation-act-1901]; Public Service Act 1999 s 7 ('Secretary') [cth-psa-1999]; Administrative Arrangements Order Part 8 [cth-aao-2025]
entries.reason: no operative provision of the Bill names the Secretary as acting or deciding anything, so no rule turns on who the Secretary is; to be revisited at 4A if the encoding finds a use

entries.to: Legislation Act 2003 Chapter 3 Part 1 (consultation, s 17), Part 2 (tabling and disallowance, ss 38-42) and Part 4 (sunsetting) [0H: cth-legislation-act-2003]; Legislation (Exemptions and Other Matters) Regulation 2015 [0H: cth-legislation-exemptions-regulation-2015]
entries.reason: no rules have been made (the Bill is not law); whether an office is prescribed under s 7(2), and what any rules provide under s 12(6), are inputs. The making and disallowance machinery decides nothing the Bill decides

entries.from: s 7(1) ('offices of the Commonwealth'), s 7(2) ('An office of the Commonwealth in a country or place outside Australia')
entries.to: Acts Interpretation Act 1901 s 21 (office etc. means office etc. of the Commonwealth) [0H: cth-acts-interpretation-act-1901]; Public Service Act 1999 s 7 ('Head of Mission': head of an Australian diplomatic or consular mission) [cth-psa-1999]
entries.reason: which office an appointment is to is an input; the encoding enumerates the s 7(1) list and takes a prescribed office (s 7(2)) as a flag

entries.from: s 8(1), s 8(2)(a) ('a member of the Parliament of the Commonwealth, the Parliament of a State or the legislature of a Territory')
entries.to: Constitution ss 7, 16, 24, 34 (membership of the Senate and House) [0H: cth-constitution]; Acts Interpretation Act 1901 s 2B ('Parliament', 'State', 'Territory') [0H: cth-acts-interpretation-act-1901]; the State constitutions and Territory self-government Acts (not held)
entries.reason: whether, and when, a person was a member of one of these legislatures is a historical fact the encoding takes as dated periods of membership; the nine bodies' own membership laws decide nothing the Bill decides

entries.from: s 8(1), s 8(2)(a) ('at any time within the last 10 years', 'at any time other than within the last 10 years')
entries.to: Acts Interpretation Act 1901 ss 36 and 37 (calculating time, expressions of time) [0H: cth-acts-interpretation-act-1901]

entries.from: s 8(2)(b) ('employed under the Members of Parliament (Staff) Act 1984 as a member of the staff of a person occupying any of the following positions')
entries.to: Members of Parliament (Staff) Act 1984 s 3 ('office-holder', 'relevant office', 'personal employee (Ministerial)', 'personal employee (non-Ministerial)', 'electorate employee', 'parliamentarian'), s 3AA (employing individual), s 4 (determination that a parliamentarian may employ personal staff), s 11 (employment of electorate and personal employees) [cth-mops-act-1984]

entries.from: s 8(2)(b) ('is or has been employed under the Members of Parliament (Staff) Act 1984')
entries.to: Members of Parliament (Staff) Act 1984 as in force before the Members of Parliament (Staff) Amendment Act 2023 and the 2026 amendments (earlier compilations: former Parts III and IV, consultants and staff of office-holders) (not held)
entries.reason: past employment is taken as a fact (employed under the Act, by whom, in which office, when); the earlier compilations are fetched only if a finding turns on how past employment under them maps onto the positions in s 8(2)(b)(i)-(vi)

entries.from: s 8(2)(b)(i) ('a Minister (including the Prime Minister)')
entries.to: Constitution s 64 (Ministers of State) [0H: cth-constitution]
entries.reason: whether the person employing the staff member held ministerial office at the time is an input

entries.from: s 8(2)(b)(ii)-(vi) (Leaders and Deputy Leaders of the Opposition in each House; 'a shadow Minister')
entries.to: Members of Parliament (Staff) Act 1984 s 3 ('relevant office' paras (b)-(e)) and s 4 [cth-mops-act-1984]; no statute defines 'shadow Minister'
entries.reason: which position the employing person occupied is an input; the Opposition offices are named in MOP(S) Act s 3 (encoded via REF-10), a shadow ministry is not a statutory office and is taken as a fact

entries.from: s 8(2)(c) ('employed under a law of a State or Territory as a member of the staff of a person occupying a position in the State or Territory that is equivalent or corresponds to a position mentioned in any of paragraphs (b)(i) to (vi)')
entries.to: the ministerial and parliamentary staff laws of the six States, the ACT and the Northern Territory (not identified, not held)
entries.reason: out of the Commonwealth Bill's own terms and eight jurisdictions wide; whether a person was so employed, and whether the position corresponds, is taken as a fact (scope 'out', lqa.json)

entries.from: s 8(2)(d) ('an officer or employee of a registered political party (within the meaning of the Commonwealth Electoral Act 1918)')
entries.to: Commonwealth Electoral Act 1918 s 4(1) ('Registered political party': registered under Part XI; 'Political party'), Part XI ss 123-126 (eligible political party, Register of Political Parties, registration) and ss 135-137 (deregistration) [cth-cea-1918-vol1]
entries.reason: whether a party is (or was, at the relevant time) on the Register of Political Parties is read from the Register, not decided; 'officer or employee' is not defined in either Act and is taken as a fact

entries.from: s 9(1) ('A person may be appointed to a designated diplomatic office only if'), s 14(1)-(3)
entries.to: Public Service Act 1999 s 39 (appointment of a Head of Mission by the Governor-General cannot take effect unless the person is an APS employee; Agency Minister's directions) and s 7 ('Head of Mission', 'Agency Minister') [cth-psa-1999]

entries.from: s 9(1), s 14(1)-(3), (7) (who makes, and who terminates, an appointment; 'a power of the Commonwealth to terminate an appointment')
entries.to: Constitution s 61 (executive power exercisable by the Governor-General), s 62-63 (Federal Executive Council; Governor-General in Council), s 64 (Ministers), s 67 (appointment and removal of other officers vested in the Governor-General in Council until Parliament provides otherwise) [0H: cth-constitution]; the prerogative power to appoint diplomatic representatives (unwritten)
entries.reason: the Bill does not say who appoints; the instruments show the Governor-General appoints Heads of Mission (Public Service Act 1999 s 39(1)), and the published practice (search-log SRCH-14, not held) is appointment by the Governor-General on Executive Council advice under the executive power. The encoding takes the appointing act and its maker as an input; whether the Bill's conditions bind that power is left to 7A and 9A

entries.from: s 9(3)(c)(ii) ('both Houses of Parliament pass a resolution approving the person's appointment')
entries.to: Constitution ss 49-50 (powers of the Houses; standing orders) [0H: cth-constitution]; Acts Interpretation Act 1901 s 47 (construction of resolutions) [0H: cth-acts-interpretation-act-1901]
entries.reason: whether each House has passed such a resolution, and when, is an event the encoding takes as input

entries.from: s 9(4) ('a statement of reasons setting out why the Minister is so satisfied')
entries.to: Acts Interpretation Act 1901 s 25D (content of statements of reasons for decisions) [0H: cth-acts-interpretation-act-1901]
entries.reason: the content of the statement is not modelled; that it was tabled, and when, is an input

entries.from: s 9(5) ('within 5 sitting days of that House after the appointment is made')
entries.to: Acts Interpretation Act 1901 s 2M (sitting day) and s 36 (calculating time) [0H: cth-acts-interpretation-act-1901]

entries.from: s 9(4)-(5) (tabling in each House)
entries.to: Acts Interpretation Act 1901 s 34B (presentation of papers to the Parliament) [0H: cth-acts-interpretation-act-1901]
entries.reason: tabling is an event taken as input; s 34B is read at 7A or 9A if a Time finding turns on presentation when a House is not sitting

entries.from: s 10(1) ('within 7 days of establishing a Selection Committee')
entries.to: Acts Interpretation Act 1901 s 36 (calculating time) [0H: cth-acts-interpretation-act-1901]

entries.from: s 10(3) ('within 2 months after receiving the list')
entries.to: Acts Interpretation Act 1901 s 2G (months) and s 36 (calculating time) [0H: cth-acts-interpretation-act-1901]

entries.from: s 10(1) ('give the Selection Committee a list'), s 10(3) ('give the Minister a written notice'), s 10(5)
entries.to: Acts Interpretation Act 1901 s 28A (service of documents) [0H: cth-acts-interpretation-act-1901]
entries.reason: when the list was given and the notice received are taken as dated events

entries.from: s 11(1) (a person 'acting in a designated diplomatic office'), s 14(4)-(6) ('An arrangement for a person to act')
entries.to: Public Service Act 1999 s 25 (assignment of duties) [cth-psa-1999]; Acts Interpretation Act 1901 s 33A (acting in offices or positions) [0H: cth-acts-interpretation-act-1901]
entries.reason: the Bill does not say who makes an acting arrangement or how; the arrangement, its maker and its period are taken as an input

entries.from: s 11 ('chargé d'affaires'); s 9 (appointment of heads of mission and consuls-general generally)
entries.to: Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations 1961 arts 4 (agrément) and 19 (chargé d'affaires ad interim), as scheduled to the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunities Act 1967; Vienna Convention on Consular Relations 1963 (not held)
entries.reason: not cited by the Bill, which defines 'chargé d'affaires' for itself in s 11(1); international law governs the receiving State's consent, not the Commonwealth's selection process (scope 'out', lqa.json)

entries.from: s 12(1) and (4) ('by written instrument'), s 12(6)(h) (termination of members), s 12(8)
entries.to: Acts Interpretation Act 1901 s 33(3) (power to make an instrument includes power to revoke or vary), s 33(4) (power to appoint includes power to remove or suspend), s 33AA (power to reappoint) [0H: cth-acts-interpretation-act-1901]
entries.reason: the establishment, membership and any revocation of a Selection Committee are taken as dated events; these sections are read at 7A or 9A if a finding turns on whether a Committee can be revoked or a member replaced

entries.from: s 12(7) ('An instrument made under subsection (1) or (4) is not a legislative instrument'); s 16(1) ('by legislative instrument')
entries.to: Legislation Act 2003 s 8 (what is a legislative instrument) [0H: cth-legislation-act-2003]

entries.from: s 13 (decision at a meeting; quorum of all 3 members; majority voting)
entries.to: Acts Interpretation Act 1901 s 33B (participation in meetings by telephone etc.) [0H: cth-acts-interpretation-act-1901]
entries.reason: whether a meeting was held, who attended and how they voted are inputs

entries.from: s 14(3), (6), (7) (termination 'as soon as practicable'; 'a power of the Commonwealth to terminate')
entries.to: Acts Interpretation Act 1901 s 33(4) [0H: cth-acts-interpretation-act-1901]; Public Service Act 1999 s 29 (termination of employment) [cth-psa-1999]; Constitution s 67 [0H: cth-constitution]
entries.reason: the Bill imposes a duty to terminate but names no power or holder; the act of termination and its maker are taken as an input, and the source of the power is left to 7A and 9A

entries.from: s 15 ('an appointment made on or after the commencement of this section if the term of the appointment starts at least 12 months after that commencement')
entries.to: Acts Interpretation Act 1901 s 3A (commencement), s 2G (months), s 36 (calculating time) [0H: cth-acts-interpretation-act-1901]
